sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 138 visitors to a science museum. She randomly selects 13 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: All 138 visitors to a science museum
Only the first 13 visitors to a science museum on a list
The researcher's own estimate
The 13 randomly selected visitors to a science museum

items.prompt: A student uses a random number generator to select 27 shoppers at a grocery store from the full list, then surveys them. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.
No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 17 students at Lincoln Middle School, 13 preferred a new park design. Based on this sample, about how many of the 102 students at Lincoln Middle School would you expect to prefer a new park design?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 15, 12, 16, 17, 15. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 1521 shoppers at a grocery store. Student A takes a random sample of 20. Student B takes a random sample of 72. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student A's sample of 20, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.
Student B's sample of 72, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.

items.prompt: A student surveys 90 visitors to a science museum using a convenience sample of her classmates only and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 1890 visitors to a science museum?
choices: Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.

items.prompt: A sample of 7 values is: 69, 93, 67, 66, 67, 72, 88. What is the range of this data set?
A data set has 6 values: 28, 25, 26, 24, 25, 25. What is the new mean if an outlier of 59 is added to the data set, making 7 values in all?
A data set is: 20, 23, 16, 37, 24, with a mean of 24. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Two data sets have means of 54 and 60. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 3. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 1 times the MAD
3 times the MAD
4 times the MAD
2 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 50, 63, 42, 49, 60, 66. Sample B: 91, 76, 67, 77, 71, 104. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample B, with a mean of 55 compared to 81.
Sample B, with a mean of 81 compared to 55.
Both samples have the same mean.
Sample A, with a mean of 55 compared to 81.

items.prompt: Sample A: 28, 10, 24, 15, 10, 28. Sample B: 27, 27, 29, 29, 25, 25. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample B, with a range of 18 compared to 4.
Both samples have the same range.
Sample A, with a range of 18 compared to 4.
Sample B, with a range of 4 compared to 18.
